assessment.overall_rationale: The sets strongly reproduce the cholesterol-biosynthetic enzyme and SREBP2 regulatory programs, while their third modules overlap more broadly in hepatic lipid handling and MASLD but emphasize different metabolic mechanisms.

pair_scores.rationale: Both modules describe the same sequential hepatic mevalonate and post-squalene cholesterol-biosynthesis pathway, with the right module adding acetyl-CoA supply and upstream sterol sensing.
They concern the same cholesterol-synthesis program, but the left centers on catalytic pathway enzymes whereas the right centers on SREBP2-dependent transcriptional control.
The modules intersect at hepatocyte cholesterol esterification through ACAT2, but the right primarily concerns downstream lipid storage, steatosis, and export rather than sterol synthesis.
The left module's SCAP-INSIG1-SREBP2 mechanism is included in the right module, but the right is primarily organized around the enzymatic biosynthesis pathway it regulates.
Both modules assert essentially the same SCAP-INSIG1-dependent SREBP2 transcriptional control of hepatic cholesterol genes, including ERG28 and RDH11.
They share a hepatic cholesterol-homeostasis and MASLD setting, but transcriptional sterol sensing and downstream lipid esterification, storage, and export are distinct mechanisms.
ACSS2-mediated acetyl-CoA provision directly feeds the biosynthetic pathway described on the right, but triglyceride synthesis and lipoprotein export are not its central mechanism.
Both relate to hepatic cholesterol homeostasis, but acetyl-CoA supply and lipid export have little mechanistic overlap with SCAP-INSIG1-SREBP2 transcriptional regulation.

Both describe MASLD-associated hepatic lipid–cholesterol coupling through DGAT2 and MTTP, although the left emphasizes ACSS2 substrate provision while the right emphasizes ACAT2 esterification and steatosis control.
